page.desc: The best smart bird feeder with camera for most yards is the Birdfy Feeder Metal 2 4K: chew-proof metal, 9,000 mAh battery with built-in solar, dual-band Wi-Fi and free lifetime bird ID. Budget and Birdbuddy alternatives compared.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best smart bird feeder with camera is the Birdfy Feeder Metal 2 4K ({buy:birdfy-feeder-metal-2-4k}): a chew-proof all-metal body, a 9,000 mAh battery with a built-in 2 W solar panel, 4K video, dual-band Wi-Fi, and since November 1, 2026 Birdfy's automatic bird ID is free for life on every Birdfy feeder. The number one complaint from owners of camera feeders is squirrels. In Tom's Guide's side-by-side test, squirrels cleaned out a plastic Birdbuddy in about a day but could not empty the Metal 2 4K through its metal grate. Whatever you buy, mount it on a pole with a baffle about 8 ft from trees; a tree strap invites squirrels and chewed cables.

Two other picks. On a budget, the Birdfy Feeder with Solar Panel ({buy:birdfy-feeder-solar-2k}) gives you 2K video, a 5,200 mAh battery, a solar panel and the same free bird ID for well under half the price. If you want close-up, bird-centered clips, the Birdfy Feeder 2 Pro ({buy:birdfy-feeder-2-pro}) adds a rotating 2K portrait lens that tracks the bird. The Birdbuddy Home has the nicer picture and the most polished app, but automatic species ID now requires a Premium membership, and its open plastic hopper is the one squirrels drained in a day.

page.after:
What owners complain about

Across reviews at MacRumors, PopSci, Tom's Guide, Trustpilot and retailer Q&A, the same five problems repeat. Squirrels come up most: MacRumors' tree-strapped Birdfy was emptied and its solar cable chewed, Tom's Guide watched squirrels drain a Birdbuddy in a day or two through its large bottom opening, and the fix in every case was a pole with a baffle about 8 ft from trees. Battery in shade is second: MacRumors' Birdfy sat near 50 percent in a wooded spot and needed a winter charge, while a sunny unit never dropped below 90 percent. Wi-Fi is third: most camera feeders are 2.4 GHz only and struggle with mesh routers and long live streams, which is why the Metal 2 4K's 5 GHz support matters. Bird ID misses: in MacRumors' 47-visit sample the Birdfy app named 38 correctly, left 14 unknown and got 2 wrong. And subscriptions: Birdbuddy moved automatic species ID behind Premium in spring 2026, while Birdfy went the other way and made it free for life for new and existing owners on November 1, 2026. Two smaller gripes: Birdfy sends an alert for every visit, often 50 or more a day, and PopSci's Birdbuddy collected water and molded seed in humid Florida.

Which one, by need

Squirrels, raccoons or a shady yard: Birdfy Feeder Metal 2 4K. Metal body, 9,000 mAh battery, built-in solar, dual-band Wi-Fi, and nothing more to pay for ID. First feeder or a gift under $150: Birdfy Feeder with Solar Panel. 2K, solar included, free ID, 2-year warranty. Close-ups and slow motion: Birdfy Feeder 2 Pro. The rotating 2K portrait lens keeps the bird centered; MacRumors wished it were sharper, so do not expect a leap over the 4K metal model. Best picture and app, no squirrels: Birdbuddy Home. Gorilla Glass 2K HDR camera, 135° view, IP67, 90-day returns, but budget for Premium if you want species named automatically.

Not recommended

Birdbuddy Nook Solar for anyone who wants automatic ID: Full HD video, a 0.9 L hopper, 2.4 GHz-only Wi-Fi and the same Premium requirement at a price close to the Birdfy 2K bundle. Birdfy Feeder 2 (non-Pro): 1080p and no solar panel in the box for more than the 2K Feeder with Solar Panel. Any plastic feeder on a tree strap in a yard with squirrels: every tester who tried it lost seed and, in two cases, the cable.
